slides.2.title: Australia's GI System Overview
slides.2.points.0: Australia uses a GI (Geographical Indication) system — not an AOC/DOC model
slides.2.points.1: Administered and certified by Wine Australia (formerly AWBC)
slides.2.points.2: Three tiers: Zone (broadest) → Region (most common on labels) → Sub-Region (most precise)
slides.2.points.4: Labelling rule: to name a GI on the label, at least 85% of the grapes must come from that GI
slides.3.title: The Three GI Tiers Compared (using Barossa as an example)
slides.3.left.label: Zone — Broadest tier
slides.3.right.label: Region — Most common on labels
slides.3.right.points.2: The most frequently seen tier on labels
slides.3.right.points.3: Roughly equivalent to a French appellation
slides.4.title: Notable Sub-Region Examples
slides.4.points.5: These Sub-Regions typically express more specific terroir than their parent Region

slides.6.title: The Label Integrity Program: Blending & Claim Rules
slides.6.points.0: Vintage claims: a single vintage requires at least 85%; multiple vintage claims must together total 100%, listed in descending order
slides.6.points.1: Variety claims: a single variety requires at least 85%; multi-variety labels must list every named variety in descending order and cannot skip a variety present in a higher proportion than one that is listed
slides.6.points.2: Example: a wine that is 70% Sémillon, 20% Chardonnay, 10% Sauvignon Blanc cannot be labelled 'Sémillon Sauvignon Blanc' (it skips the larger Chardonnay component) — it must read 'Sémillon Chardonnay' or list all three
slides.6.points.3: GI claims: a single GI requires at least 85%; up to 3 GIs can be claimed together, must total at least 95%, each named GI must exceed 5% of the blend, listed in descending order
slides.6.points.4: This is the Label Integrity Program (LIP), overseen by Wine Australia to keep label claims traceable and auditable
slides.7.question: If an Australian wine label states 'Barossa Valley', which GI tier does this represent?
slides.7.explanation: Barossa Valley is a GI Region — its parent Zone is Barossa Zone, which is distinct from Barossa Valley itself.
slides.8.title: Lesson Summary
slides.8.points.0: Australia uses a GI system (not AOC/DOC): three tiers — Zone → Region → Sub-Region
slides.8.points.1: Region is the tier most commonly seen on labels (e.g. Barossa Valley, Margaret River)
slides.8.points.2: Naming a GI on the label requires at least 85% of grapes from that GI
slides.8.points.3: The Label Integrity Program further governs the percentages and ordering rules for vintage, variety and multi-GI claims
